title: The Unforgivable Sin
lead: Jesus' warning that blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven (Matthew 12:31–32; Mark 3:28–30; Luke 12:10), spoken when opponents said his exorcisms were done by Beelzebul. Christians have long asked what this sin is and whether a believer can commit it.

sections.b: Mark explains the saying: Jesus spoke this way "because their claim was, 'He has an unclean spirit'" (Mark 3:30). Matthew sets it after the Pharisees' charge that Jesus drives out demons by Beelzebul (Matthew 12:24) and adds that a word against the Son of Man can be forgiven. Luke places it in a different setting, about disciples on trial (Luke 12:10). Related warnings appear in Hebrews 6:4–6 and 1 John 5:16. Most interpreters agree that the sin is not a single careless word but a settled refusal of God's work, and that it is unforgivable because the one who commits it does not repent.
